changelog.change: First draft for editorial review: 66 interventions, 104 test rows, 12 draft human-evidence grades.

method.primary_test: The ITP's pre-specified primary analysis: a log-rank test comparing treated and control mice of the same sex, stratified by test site, with data pooled across the three sites.
method.significance: Extended or shortened = p < 0.05 in that analysis.
method.trend_rule: Trend = 0.05 ≤ p < 0.10, direction from the median change. Not statistically significant.
method.verdict_rule: Both sexes: extended in males and females (in any cohort) with no shortening. Males only / Females only: extended in one sex only, no shortening. Mixed: extended in some test but shortened in another sex or test. Shortened: shortened with no extension. No effect: neither.
method.replication_rule: Replicated: extended in the same sex in two or more cohort years. Not reproduced: extended once, but a later test in that sex (any dose or start age) found no benefit. Single cohort: extended once, not retested.
method.median_change: Percent change in median lifespan versus same-sex controls, as reported in the cited paper (null when not reported or not captured).
method.reanalysis_policy: Verdicts follow the ITP's own primary analysis. Later reanalyses are shown separately and never change the verdict.

verdict_descriptions.both: Longer life in males and in females
verdict_descriptions.males: Longer life in males; no extension in females
verdict_descriptions.females: Longer life in females; no extension in males
verdict_descriptions.mixed: Longer life in one sex or test, shorter in another
verdict_descriptions.none: No significant change in either sex
verdict_descriptions.shortened: Shorter life, with no extension in any test

replication.replicated: Replicated: extended in the same sex in two or more cohort years.
replication.not_reproduced: Not reproduced: a later test in the same sex found no benefit.
replication.single_cohort: Single cohort: extended once and not retested.

strong.label: Strong
strong.definition: Randomized controlled trials in humans show benefit on hard clinical outcomes (mortality or major disease events).

plausible_weak.label: Plausible but weak
plausible_weak.definition: Some human evidence (small or short trials on biomarkers or surrogate endpoints, or consistent observational data) plus a credible mechanism.

not_supported.label: Not supported
not_supported.definition: Human trials tested it and found no benefit, or the evidence points to harm.

not_graded.label: Not yet graded
not_graded.definition: LEV has not reviewed the human evidence yet.

compounds.name: Metformin
compounds.mechanism: Lowers glucose output from the liver; mildly slows mitochondrial energy production, activating cellular energy-stress signals (AMPK).
compounds.meaning: No lifespan extension in the ITP's main analysis; a later reanalysis suggests a modest midlife benefit in males. Either way, the mouse data are far weaker than metformin's reputation.

cohorts.test: Log-rank, stratified by site; 3 sites pooled; each sex separately

verification.note: Result, dose and start age read from the cited paper.

reanalyses.finding: A 2024 reanalysis using the Gehan test found a significant survival benefit in males (p = 0.0495, median about 8%), concentrated in early and middle life; no effect in females.

compounds.explainer: Two statistical tests, two readings. The ITP's standard test (log-rank) counts deaths at every age equally and works best when a drug cuts the death rate by the same proportion throughout life. The Gehan test gives more weight to earlier deaths, when more mice are still alive. Metformin-treated males died less often in middle age but not late in life, so the curves separate early and then converge: that pattern passes the Gehan test (p = 0.0495) but not the log-rank test (p = 0.35). Because the reanalysis was a secondary look across 132 comparisons and lands right at the 0.05 line, LEV treats it as a lead worth testing, not a result.

popular.reason: Widely taken off-label for longevity; proposed for the TAME aging trial.
